perf.summary: Replace signed (i-1)/2 parent computation with unsigned shift to drop the signed-division sign-correction sequence in the A* heap hot path.
perf.currentCost: `parent = (i - 1) / 2` divides a signed int by 2. Because the compiler cannot prove (i-1) is non-negative, it emits the full signed-divide-by-constant idiom (shift + sign-bit add/cmov), roughly 3-4 extra ops per loop iteration, executed once per heap level on every Push and every Pop's final BubbleUp.
perf.proposedChange: Compute the parent as `int parent = (int)((uint)(i - 1) >> 1);` (or keep `i` and write `(i - 1) >> 1` only once i>0 is guaranteed). Since the loop body only runs while `i > 0`, `i - 1 >= 0`, so an unsigned `>> 1` is exactly `(i-1)/2`. Hoist the first `parent` computation inside/after the `i>0` guard so the initial pre-loop computation (where i could be 0 -> (i-1) = -1) is never division-corrected.
perf.rationale: For non-negative operands, arithmetic `/2` and logical `>>1` produce identical results, but `>>1` is a single-cycle op versus the multi-op signed-division-by-constant lowering. This runs O(log n) times per heap operation and the heap operation count dominates A* search.
perf.risk: Pre-loop `parent = (i-1)/2` with i==0 yields (-1)/2 == 0 in signed, but `(uint)(-1)>>1` == 0x7FFFFFFF. That value is only consumed inside the loop guarded by `i>0`, so it is never dereferenced — still, to be safe, only compute parent after confirming i>0 (move it to loop end / use the guarded form). With that guard the change is exactly semantics-preserving.

perf.summary: Replace signed (i*2)+1 child index with unsigned shift, and reduce the dependency chain on heap[child]->total reloads.
perf.currentCost: `child = (i * 2) + 1` uses signed multiply (cheap) but pairs with the BubbleUp signed-div issue; more importantly each iteration does two pointer-chasing loads `heap[child]->total` and `heap[child+1]->total` that feed a branch. Runs O(log n) per Pop.
perf.proposedChange: Use `int child = ((int)((uint)i << 1)) | 1;` (i>=0 so `i<<1` cannot overflow into sign within valid heap sizes). Cache `float tChild = this.heap[child]->total;` once and compare against `this.heap[child+1]->total` so the chosen child's total is reused by the subsequent `BubbleUp(i, node)` comparison path where possible; at minimum avoid recomputing `i*2+1` twice by reusing a local.
perf.rationale: `<<1 | 1` is branch-free integer arithmetic matching `i*2+1` for non-negative i. Caching the total of the selected child removes a redundant dependent load before the swap store. Both shave fixed cycles per heap level on the Pop critical path.
perf.risk: Multiplication semantics are identical for in-range i; the only caveat is overflow if i were near int.MAX, which is impossible since child<size<=capacity (a reasonable node count). No observable behavior change.

perf.summary: Mark the private heap helpers (and Push/Pop) AggressiveInlining so the hot A* loop avoids call overhead.
perf.currentCost: `BubbleUp` and `TrickleDown` are private leaf-ish methods called from Push/Pop/Modify with no inlining hint. Top() has the hint but Push/Pop/BubbleUp/TrickleDown do not. Each Push/Pop incurs a call frame plus the helper call frame.
perf.proposedChange: Add `[MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)]` to `BubbleUp` and `TrickleDown` (and optionally Push/Pop). Under Burst these become straight-line code with the loop bodies inlined into the caller, enabling register allocation of `size`/`heap` across the boundary.
perf.rationale: Removing the call boundary lets Burst/LLVM keep `this.heap`, `this.size`, and the node pointer in registers and fuse the BubbleUp tail-call inside TrickleDown, cutting prologue/epilogue and spill traffic on the search hot path.
perf.risk: Pure inlining hint; no semantic change. Slight code-size growth, acceptable on the A* hot path.

perf.summary: Modify is an O(n) linear scan over the heap to locate a node before re-bubbling; flag as a structural cost.
perf.currentCost: `for i in 0..size: if heap[i]==node` is O(n) per call. In A* with node re-relaxation this is called per improved neighbor, making the queue-update path O(n) instead of O(log n).
perf.proposedChange: Store the heap slot index back into the DtNode (it already has spare reserved bits in packedData, or use State-adjacent storage) so Modify can jump directly to the node's slot and call BubbleUp in O(log n). Maintaining the index requires updating it on every store in BubbleUp/TrickleDown. If the API/struct cannot change, leave as-is — this is a design tradeoff, not a free win.
perf.rationale: Reduces Modify from O(n) to O(log n), turning the dominant re-relaxation cost in dense graphs from linear to logarithmic.
perf.risk: Requires writing the slot index on every heap store (extra writes in BubbleUp/TrickleDown) and a free bit in DtNode; if those stores outweigh the scan for small heaps it can regress. Not semantics-preserving for the struct layout — only viable if DtNode gains/uses a heap-index field. Propose only as an opt-in design change.
